Hydration is just water as a share of flour. Once you see it, you can't unsee it.

instances.html:
Compound Interest Formula

The quiet engine behind every "start early" lecture you've ever received.

A = P (1 + r / n)n t

P is your starting pot, r the annual rate as a decimal, n how often it compounds per year, t the years. £1,000 at 5% monthly for 10 years lands near £1,647.

  1. Write the rate as a decimal: 5% → 0.05.
  2. Divide by compounds per year: 0.05 / 12 ≈ 0.004167.
  3. Add 1, raise to (n × t) = 120.
  4. Multiply by your starting amount.
Why does frequency matter?

More compounding periods means interest earns interest sooner. The difference is small monthly vs yearly, but it adds up over decades.

  3. Pour hot (not boiling) water to that mark, leaving the calculated air gap.
  4. Squeeze gently to check for give — a healthy gap feels springy, not stiff.
